source.title_on_document: Inquiry-based learning in STEM education: the impact of generative AI-based Chatbots on primary school students' problem posing ability in science

supplement.where: Online version at https://doi.org/10.1186/s40594-026-00631-0, Additional file 1 and Additional file 2 (p. 19, Supplementary Information)
supplement.holds: Additional file 1: final versions of problem posing Tests 1 and 2 (p. 9). Additional file 2: baseline (pre-test) between-group comparisons and within-group pre/post test results, plus ENA visualizations of baseline and within-group pre/post changes (p. 13). The post-test between-group statistics are in the main text (Table 5).

paper_design_summary: Two intact third-grade classes (97 students, aged 8-9) at one primary school in central China took part; one class was randomly selected to use a custom GLM-4 chatbot (Question Pot) and the other used the Baidu search engine during three problem-based inquiry lessons on the Air unit. Students took a 15-minute paper problem posing test before (Test 1) and after (Test 2) the intervention; two researchers coded each question for number, category, and quality (Bloom level), which were combined into a 10-point problem posing ability score. Classroom questions from the chatbot dialogues and search records were also coded and modeled with epistemic network analysis, and students answered cognitive load and technology acceptance questionnaires.

studies.label: Two-class quasi-experiment: GLM-4 chatbot vs Baidu search in third-grade science problem posing

assignment.what_was_assigned: Technology condition (chatbot vs search engine) for the problem-based inquiry lessons, assigned to whole classes: one of two classes was randomly selected as the experimental group
assignment.quote: One class was randomly selected as the experimental group (N = 48), and the other as the control group (N = 49), with technology conditions allocated at the class level.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Methods, Participants; also p. 1, Abstract ("randomly assigned by class")

arms.name: Experimental group (chatbot)
arms.description: Used Question Pot, a custom agent built on the ChatGLM platform with the GLM-4 model, on tablets during the three problem-based inquiry lessons, through multi-round dialogue to generate and refine questions

arms.name: Control group (search engine)
arms.description: Used the Baidu search engine on tablets during the same inquiry lessons, relying on keyword retrieval and reading to develop questions

participants.exclusions: 185 test papers were collected. 90 valid pre-tests (46 experimental, 44 control) entered the baseline analysis. Pre/post and post-test analyses kept only students with complete pre- and post-test participation: 89 (45 experimental, 44 control), i.e., 8 of 97 students (3 experimental, 5 control) not analyzed; reasons beyond the pairing rule are not given. Questionnaires: 93 collected, 7 excluded for missing data or straightlining, 86 analyzed (42 experimental, 44 control).
participants.who: Third-grade primary school students aged 8-9, two classes at one school
participants.quote: The final number of valid samples included in the analyses was 89 (45 in the experimental group and 44 in the control group).
participants.locator: p. 12, Data analysis; p. 13, Results; p. 13, Table 5 (N = 89)

ai_tool.name_model: Question Pot, custom agent on the ChatGLM platform using the GLM-4 model
ai_tool.how_used: Scaffolding chatbot configured per topic (Table 2): teaches questioning strategies, guides follow-up questions and question chains, encourages cross-disciplinary questions. It also offered example questions in all topics and follow-up question suggestions in Topic 1 only (disabled from Topic 2 to stop students copying questions); a motivational 'Smart Star' mechanism was added in Topics 2-3. Used on tablets only during the problem-based inquiry lessons (pp. 6, 8, Table 2).

task.description: Science problem posing: students pose as many questions as they can (questions only, no answers) about three short science passages (two text, one text plus image). Post-test (Test 2) items were from the Air unit: air movement forms wind, air can be compressed, applications of air in daily life (pp. 8-9).
task.duration: Tests: 15 minutes each. Intervention: three rounds of thematic inquiry, each with several regular lessons and one problem-based inquiry lesson; calendar length not stated (pp. 6, 8).

outcomes.name: Post-test total problem posing ability score (0-10)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Sum of number (weight 3), category (weight 2), and quality (weight 5) scores computed from rubric codes assigned to each question by two trained researchers (kappa 0.886 on pilot, 0.827 on 20 percent of study data; disagreements resolved by discussion) (pp. 10-12, Table 3, Eqs. 1-4).
outcomes.delay: Not stated in days; post-test is stage 5, after the three inquiry rounds (Fig. 1, p. 6)

contrasts.reported: Experimental M = 5.80 (SD 0.59, N = 45) vs control M = 5.36 (SD 0.73, N = 44); t = 3.07, df = 82.61 (adjusted for unequal variances), p = 0.003, Cohen's d = 0.65

outcomes.name: Post-test quality score (Bloom cognitive level of questions)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each question coded on a five-level scale adapted from revised Bloom taxonomy (remembering/understanding 1, applying 2, analyzing 3, evaluating 4, creating 5); weighted average per student, rescaled to a 5-point maximum (pp. 10-11, Table 3, Eq. 4).
outcomes.delay: Not stated in days; post-test after the three inquiry rounds

contrasts.reported: Experimental M = 2.46 (SD 0.26, N = 45) vs control M = 2.29 (SD 0.35, N = 44); t = 2.47, df = 87, p = 0.015, Cohen's d = 0.52

outcomes.name: Post-test number score (count of valid questions, banded)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Total count of valid questions per student, excluding non-interrogative statements, banded into levels L1 (<= 5) to L5 (>= 20) and scored as level x 0.6 (pp. 10-11, Table 3, Eq. 2).
outcomes.delay: Not stated in days; post-test after the three inquiry rounds

contrasts.reported: Experimental M = 2.12 (SD 0.57, N = 45) vs control M = 1.92 (SD 0.65, N = 44); t = 1.52, df = 87, p = 0.132, Cohen's d = 0.32

outcomes.name: Post-test category score (weighted question-type score)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each question coded into six types with point values (irrelevant 0, context-based 1, learned knowledge 2, real-life 3, other-discipline 1, comprehensive 2); weighted average per student rescaled to a 2-point maximum (pp. 10-11, Table 3, Eq. 3). This is a weighted average of type scores, not a count of distinct categories.
outcomes.delay: Not stated in days; post-test after the three inquiry rounds

contrasts.reported: Experimental M = 1.22 (SD 0.15, N = 45) vs control M = 1.15 (SD 0.24, N = 44); t = 1.76, df = 73.72 (adjusted for unequal variances), p = 0.082, Cohen's d = 0.38

outcomes.name: Post-test epistemic network structure of question category and quality codes
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Epistemic network analysis (epistemicnetwork.org) of co-occurrences among 11 category and quality codes; group mean networks and a subtracted network (pp. 12-14, Fig. 3).
outcomes.delay: Not stated in days; post-test after the three inquiry rounds

contrasts.reported: Descriptive only: experimental group network broader and higher-density, with stronger connections around SL, SR, P, and E; control group connections cluster around R (R-SC, R-P). No test statistic in the main text.

outcomes.name: Epistemic network structure of questions posed during the inquiry lessons (with tools)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Questions from Question Pot dialogue records and Baidu search records coded for category and quality (quantity not coded and no ability scores computed for this phase), then modeled as ENA mean networks and centroid trajectories across Topics 1-3 (pp. 11-14, Fig. 4).

contrasts.reported: Descriptive only: experimental group network expanded and deepened across topics with more nodes participating; control group showed localized changes in connection strength with node count unchanged. No test statistic.

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1: the condition was assigned at random, but only between two intact classes (one class per arm), so treatment is confounded with class and the paper itself calls the design quasi-experimental (pp. 1, 5); whether a two-cluster random selection counts as random assignment of people is for Review 1. If not, the study is quasi_people context (observational). Criterion 2: 97 assigned, 89 analyzed (45 vs 44), well above 50. Criterion 3: researcher-coded problem posing scores on students' questions (number of questions is a fluency measure; quality and category are rubric scores); the main outcomes are measured on a paper post-test after the chatbot period, so they answer after_ai. The comparison arm is a search engine (ai_vs_active).

one_line_finding: On a paper post-test taken after three inquiry lessons, the chatbot class outscored the search-engine class on total problem posing ability (5.80 vs 5.36, t = 3.07, p = 0.003, d = 0.65) and question quality (2.46 vs 2.29, p = 0.015), with no significant difference in number or category (p. 13, Table 5).
open_questions: Does a random choice between two intact classes (one per arm) satisfy criterion 1, or should this be coded quasi_people/observational?

The paper does not state explicitly that tablets and tools were unavailable during the post-test; coding as after_ai rests on the post-test being a separate 15-minute paper test (stage 5 in Fig. 1, '185 test papers', researcher monitoring).
Is problem posing ability (rubric of number, category, and Bloom level) close enough to creativity for this section, or should only the number-of-questions (fluency) outcome count?
Standard errors and t-tests treat students as independent although assignment is at the class level with one class per arm.
notes: Self-reported cognitive load (8 items) and technology acceptance (13 items) questionnaires were also compared (pp. 14-15, Figs. 5-6; n = 86) but are not scored on output and are not listed as outcomes. Baseline equivalence (90 pre-tests, no significant differences, p > 0.05) and within-group pre/post results are in Additional file 2, not in this PDF. Class-level equivalence on prior-semester science exam scores is reported only as a non-significant t-test (p. 5). The same teacher taught both classes. Total coded entries: 3010 (p. 12).
